records.source: וַתְּהִ֤י הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ אֲרֻכָּ֔ה בֵּ֚ין בֵּ֣ית שָׁא֔וּל וּבֵ֖ין בֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֑ד וְדָוִד֙ הֹלֵ֣ךְ וְחָזֵ֔ק וּבֵ֥ית שָׁא֖וּל הֹלְכִ֥ים וְדַלִּֽים׃ס
records.gloss: And was the war long between [the] house of Saul and between [the] house of David; and David [was] going and strong, and [the] house of Saul [were] going and weak.
pieces: The war between Saul's house and David's house dragged on for a long time. David grew steadily stronger, while the house of Saul grew steadily weaker.

L.1: And the war between the house of Saul and the house of David was long. And David went on growing strong, and the house of Saul went on growing weak.

R.1: The war between Saul's family and David's family lasted a long time. David's side kept getting stronger, and Saul's side kept getting weaker.

decisions.choice: the house of Saul, the house of David: each man's family and the people who supported his claim to rule
decisions.reason: "House" here means a royal family together with its followers. On one side stood Saul's son Ish-bosheth, made king by Abner (2:8-10); on the other stood David, king in Hebron over Judah (2:4).

decisions.choice: going and strong, going and weak: growing steadily stronger and steadily weaker
decisions.reason: The verb "go" joined to another word describes something that keeps on happening and increasing (Genesis 26:13; 1 Samuel 14:19). The verse sums up the years of war after 2:11 before Abner changes sides.

decisions.choice: Saul's family, David's family; David's side, Saul's side
decisions.reason: Readable says "family" and "side" so that "house" is not taken to mean a building.

records.source: וַיִּוָּלְד֧וּלְדָוִ֛ד בָּנִ֖ים בְּחֶבְר֑וֹן וַיְהִ֤י בְכוֹרוֹ֙ אַמְנ֔וֹן לַאֲחִינֹ֖עַם הַיִּזְרְעֵאלִֽת׃
records.gloss: And were born to David sons in Hebron; and was his firstborn Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelite.
pieces: Sons were born to David in Hebron. His firstborn was Amnon, whose mother was Ahinoam of Jezreel.

L.2: And sons were born to David in Hebron. And his firstborn was Amnon, by Ahinoam the Jezreelite.

R.2: While David was in Hebron, sons were born to him. The oldest was Amnon, and his mother was Ahinoam from the town of Jezreel.

decisions.choice: were born: the reading noted in the margin
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text give a slightly different form of the verb from the one the scribes noted in the margin. Both mean that sons were born, and the meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: a list of the sons born at Hebron
decisions.reason: Verses 2-5 break into the story of the war to list David's six sons born during his seven and a half years in Hebron (2:11). 1 Chronicles 3:1-4 gives the same list. Several of these sons matter later: Amnon (chapter 13), Absalom (chapters 13-18) and Adonijah (1 Kings 1).

decisions.choice: Ahinoam the Jezreelite: from the Jezreel in Judah
decisions.reason: David married Ahinoam while he was on the run from Saul (1 Samuel 25:43). Her town is most likely the Jezreel in the hill country of Judah (Joshua 15:56), not the better-known Jezreel in the north.

decisions.choice: whose mother was (Balanced); his mother was (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "of Ahinoam" or "by Ahinoam". Balanced and Readable say plainly that she was the boy's mother, and the list keeps the same wording for each son.

records.heading: Sons born to David in Hebron

records.source: וּמִשְׁנֵ֣הוּ כִלְאָ֔ב לַאֲֽבִיגַ֕יִלאֵ֖שֶׁת נָבָ֣ל הַֽכַּרְמְלִ֑י וְהַשְּׁלִשִׁי֙ אַבְשָׁל֣וֹם בֶּֽן־מַעֲכָ֔ה בַּת־תַּלְמַ֖י מֶ֥לֶךְ גְּשֽׁוּר׃
records.gloss: And his second Chileab, of Abigail [the] wife of Nabal the Carmelite; and the third Absalom son of Maacah daughter of Talmai king of Geshur.
pieces: His second was Chileab, whose mother was Abigail, the widow of Nabal of Carmel. The third was Absalom, whose mother was Maacah daughter of Talmai king of Geshur.

L.3: And his second [was] Chileab, by Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite; and the third, Absalom son of Maacah daughter of Talmai king of Geshur.

R.3: His second son was Chileab, and his mother was Abigail, who had been the wife of Nabal from Carmel. The third son was Absalom, and his mother was Maacah. She was the daughter of Talmai, the king of Geshur.

decisions.choice: Abigail: the reading noted in the margin
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text spell Abigail's name in a shorter form; the scribes' marginal reading gives the usual spelling, as in 1 Samuel 25. It is the same woman.

decisions.choice: Chileab: called Daniel in the parallel list
decisions.reason: 1 Chronicles 3:1 names David's second son "Daniel". He may have had two names. Nothing more is told of him.

decisions.choice: the wife of Nabal: Abigail had been Nabal's wife until his death
decisions.reason: Nabal died soon after Abigail met David, and David then married her (1 Samuel 25:37-42). The list still names her by her first husband.

decisions.choice: Talmai king of Geshur: a small kingdom northeast of Israel
decisions.reason: Geshur was a small Aramean kingdom east of the Sea of Galilee, which Israel had never driven out (Joshua 13:13). Marrying a king's daughter made an alliance. Absalom later fled to his grandfather Talmai (13:37-38).

decisions.choice: the widow of Nabal (Balanced); who had been the wife of Nabal (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "wife of Nabal". Since Nabal had died before she married David, Balanced says "widow" and Readable "had been the wife", so that readers do not think she was still married to him.

records.source: וְהָרְבִיעִ֖י אֲדֹנִיָּ֣ה בֶן־חַגִּ֑ית וְהַחֲמִישִׁ֖י שְׁפַטְיָ֥ה בֶן־אֲבִיטָֽל׃
records.gloss: And the fourth Adonijah son of Haggith; and the fifth Shephatiah son of Abital.
pieces: The fourth was Adonijah, whose mother was Haggith, and the fifth was Shephatiah, whose mother was Abital.

L.4: And the fourth [was] Adonijah son of Haggith; and the fifth, Shephatiah son of Abital.

R.4: The fourth son was Adonijah, and his mother was Haggith. The fifth son was Shephatiah, and his mother was Abital.

decisions.choice: son of Haggith, son of Abital: named by their mothers
decisions.reason: In a household with several wives, sons of the same father were told apart by their mothers. The list names each son's mother, as in verses 2-3.

decisions.choice: Adonijah: the son who later tried to take the throne
decisions.reason: When David was old, Adonijah, as the oldest living son, claimed the kingdom, and is still called "son of Haggith" there (1 Kings 1:5).

decisions.choice: whose mother was (Balanced); his mother was (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

records.source: וְהַשִּׁשִּׁ֣י יִתְרְעָ֔ם לְעֶגְלָ֖ה אֵ֣שֶׁת דָּוִ֑ד אֵ֛לֶּה יֻלְּד֥וּ לְדָוִ֖ד בְּחֶבְרֽוֹן׃פ
records.gloss: And the sixth Ithream, of Eglah [the] wife of David. These were born to David in Hebron.
pieces: The sixth was Ithream, whose mother was Eglah, David's wife. These sons were born to David in Hebron.

L.5: And the sixth [was] Ithream, by Eglah, David's wife. These were born to David in Hebron.

R.5: The sixth son was Ithream, and his mother was Eglah, another of David's wives. These six sons were born to David while he was in Hebron.

decisions.choice: Eglah, David's wife
decisions.reason: All six women were David's wives, but only Eglah is called "David's wife" here. The text does not say why; the words may simply round off the list. 1 Chronicles 3:3 says the same.

decisions.choice: these were born to David in Hebron: the end of the list
decisions.reason: The closing words repeat the opening of verse 2, marking where the list ends and the story of Abner takes up again.

decisions.choice: another of David's wives; these six sons
decisions.reason: Readable adds "another of" so that Eglah is not taken to be David's only wife, and gives the number of sons the list has named.

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י בִּֽהְיוֹת֙ הַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה בֵּ֚ין בֵּ֣ית שָׁא֔וּל וּבֵ֖ין בֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֑ד וְאַבְנֵ֛ר הָיָ֥ה מִתְחַזֵּ֖ק בְּבֵ֥ית שָׁאֽוּל׃
records.gloss: And it was, while was the war between [the] house of Saul and between [the] house of David, and Abner was making himself strong in [the] house of Saul.
pieces: While the war went on between the house of Saul and the house of David, Abner was steadily building up his own power in the house of Saul.

L.6: And it happened, while there was war between the house of Saul and the house of David, that Abner was making himself strong in the house of Saul.

R.6: During the war between Saul's family and David's family, Abner was making himself more and more powerful among Saul's people.

decisions.choice: while there was war: the story picks up again from verse 1
decisions.reason: After the list of sons, these words take up the war of verse 1 again and lead into what happened between Abner and Ish-bosheth.

decisions.choice: making himself strong: strengthening his own position
alternatives: holding firmly to the house of Saul
giving strong support to the house of Saul
decisions.reason: The form of the verb means "to make oneself strong". It can describe loyal effort on behalf of Saul's house, but here it most likely means that Abner was gathering power for himself within it, which is the background to Ish-bosheth's charge in verse 7.

decisions.choice: his own power (Balanced); more and more powerful (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that the strength Abner was building was his own; see the meaning decision on these words.

records.heading: Abner goes over to David

records.source: וּלְשָׁא֣וּל פִּלֶ֔גֶשׁ וּשְׁמָ֖הּ רִצְפָּ֣ה בַת־אַיָּ֑ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־אַבְנֵ֔ר מַדּ֥וּעַ בָּ֖אתָה אֶל־פִּילֶ֥גֶשׁ אָבִֽי׃
records.gloss: And to Saul [was] a concubine, and her name [was] Rizpah daughter of Aiah; and he said to Abner, Why have you gone in to [the] concubine of my father?
pieces: Now Saul had had a concubine named Rizpah daughter of Aiah. Ish-bosheth said to Abner, "Why have you slept with my father's concubine?"

L.7: Now Saul had a concubine, and her name [was] Rizpah daughter of Aiah. And he said to Abner, "Why have you gone in to my father's concubine?"

R.7: Saul had had a concubine (a secondary wife) named Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah. Ish-bosheth said to Abner, "Why did you sleep with my father's concubine?"

decisions.choice: concubine: a wife of lower rank
decisions.reason: A concubine was a wife with fewer rights than a full wife, often without a bride-price, and her children did not always inherit. Rizpah had two sons by Saul (21:8).

decisions.choice: taking a dead king's concubine: a claim to his throne
decisions.reason: A new king took over his predecessor's household, including his wives (12:8). For another man to take a dead king's concubine could be read as a claim to rule (16:21-22; 1 Kings 2:22). So Ish-bosheth's question is an accusation of disloyalty, not only of wrongdoing.

decisions.choice: and he said: the speaker is not named
decisions.reason: The traditional Hebrew text says only "and he said". Some ancient witnesses add the name Ish-bosheth, Saul's son, and the next verse makes clear that he is the speaker.

decisions.choice: gone in to: had sexual relations with
decisions.reason: "Go in to" a woman is a common way of speaking of sexual relations (Genesis 16:2; 29:23).

decisions.choice: Ish-bosheth said
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker, as verse 8 does, so the reader is not left to guess.

decisions.choice: concubine (a secondary wife)
decisions.reason: As set for these books, Readable explains "concubine" the first time it appears in a chapter.

records.source: וַיִּחַר֩ לְאַבְנֵ֨ר מְאֹ֜ד עַל־דִּבְרֵ֣י אִֽישׁ־בֹּ֗שֶׁת וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הֲרֹ֨אשׁ כֶּ֥לֶב אָנֹ֘כִי֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לִֽיהוּדָה֒ הַיּ֨וֹם אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־חֶ֜סֶד עִם־בֵּ֣ית׀שָׁא֣וּל אָבִ֗יךָ אֶל־אֶחָיו֙ וְאֶל־מֵ֣רֵעֵ֔הוּ וְלֹ֥א הִמְצִיתִ֖ךָ בְּיַד־דָּוִ֑ד וַתִּפְקֹ֥ד עָלַ֛י עֲוֺ֥ן הָאִשָּׁ֖ה הַיּֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: And burned to Abner exceedingly over [the] words of Ish-bosheth, and he said, [Am] I a dog's head which [belongs] to Judah? This day I show steadfast love to [the] house of Saul your father, to his brothers and to his friends, and I have not caused you to be found in [the] hand of David; and you charge on me [the] guilt of the woman today.
pieces: Abner was furious at Ish-bosheth's words. "Am I a dog's head on Judah's side?" he said. "To this day I have kept faithful love toward the house of your father Saul, toward his brothers and his friends, and I have not let you fall into David's hands. And now you charge me with wrongdoing over this woman!

L.8: And Abner was very angry over the words of Ish-bosheth, and he said, "[Am] I a dog's head that [belongs] to Judah? This day I show steadfast love to the house of Saul your father, to his brothers and to his friends, and I have not let you fall into the hand of David; and you charge me today with guilt over the woman!

R.8: Abner became very angry at what Ish-bosheth said. He answered, "Do you think I am a worthless dog who works for Judah? All this time I have shown faithful love to your father Saul's family, his relatives and his friends. I have not let David capture you. And now you accuse me of doing wrong with this woman!

decisions.choice: a dog's head: something utterly worthless and despised
alternatives: the leader of a pack of dogs
decisions.reason: The phrase appears only here. Dogs were scavengers, and to call someone a dog was an insult (1 Samuel 17:43; 24:15; 2 Samuel 9:8; 16:9). "A dog's head" seems to sharpen the insult: the most contemptible thing there is. Abner asks whether Ish-bosheth takes him for a worthless traitor, after all he has done for Saul's house. The exact picture is not certain.

decisions.choice: that belongs to Judah
decisions.reason: These words, which make Abner's question "Am I a traitor working for Judah?", are not found in the ancient Greek translation. The Hebrew text has them, and they fit Abner's point: he has fought against Judah, not for it.

decisions.choice: steadfast love: loyalty owed under a bond
decisions.reason: The word names faithful, committed loyalty, the kind owed within a family or by a covenant. Abner claims that loyalty for himself: he has held Saul's house together.

decisions.choice: I have not let you fall into the hand of David: I have not handed you over to David
decisions.reason: The verb means "cause to be found" in someone's hand, that is, to deliver someone to an enemy's power. Abner reminds Ish-bosheth that his throne depends on Abner.

decisions.choice: you charge me with guilt over the woman: Abner neither denies nor admits the act
decisions.reason: Abner does not say whether he took Rizpah. He treats the charge itself as an insult to his loyalty.

decisions.choice: steadfast love (Literal); faithful love (Balanced and Readable)
decisions.reason: As set for these books, following Exodus 34:6.

decisions.choice: a dog's head on Judah's side (Balanced); a worthless dog who works for Judah (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the unusual picture and makes the relative clause plain; Readable says what the picture means.

records.source: כֹּֽה־יַעֲשֶׂ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙ לְאַבְנֵ֔ר וְכֹ֖ה יֹסִ֣יף ל֑וֹ כִּ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר נִשְׁבַּ֤ע יְהוָה֙ לְדָוִ֔ד כִּֽי־כֵ֖ן אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־לּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Thus may do God to Abner, and thus may he add to him, for as swore Yahweh to David, so I will do for him,
pieces: May God deal with me, Abner, ever so severely if I fail to carry out for David what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} promised him on oath,

L.9: Thus may God do to Abner, and thus may {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} add to him, for as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has sworn to David, so I will do for him,

R.9: I will now do for David what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} promised him with an oath. If I do not, may God punish me terribly.

decisions.choice: thus may God do to Abner, and thus may he add: a curse on oneself
decisions.reason: This is the form of a solemn oath: the speaker calls down punishment on himself if he fails to keep his word (1 Samuel 3:17; 20:13; verse 35). Abner speaks of himself by name.

decisions.choice: as Yahweh has sworn to David: Abner knows that Yahweh has chosen David
decisions.reason: Yahweh had rejected Saul and chosen David (1 Samuel 15:28; 16:1-13; 25:30). No oath in these exact words is recorded, but Abner speaks of the promise as known. His words show that he has been fighting against what he knew Yahweh had promised.

decisions.choice: for as ... so I will do: the content of the oath
decisions.reason: The sentence runs into verse 10, which says what Abner will do. In an oath like this, the words mean "I will surely do it".

decisions.choice: May God deal with me, Abner, ever so severely
decisions.reason: As in 1 Samuel 20:13, Balanced keeps Abner's name but makes clear that he is the speaker.

decisions.choice: I will now do ... If I do not, may God punish me
decisions.reason: Readable puts the promise first and the curse after it, so that the oath is easy to follow.

records.source: לְהַֽעֲבִ֥יר הַמַּמְלָכָ֖ה מִבֵּ֣ית שָׁא֑וּל וּלְהָקִ֞ים אֶת־כִּסֵּ֣א דָוִ֗ד עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְעַל־יְהוּדָ֔ה מִדָּ֖ן וְעַד־בְּאֵ֥ר שָֽׁבַע׃
records.gloss: to transfer the kingdom from [the] house of Saul, and to establish [the] throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan and to Beersheba.
pieces: by taking the kingdom from the house of Saul and setting up David's throne over Israel and Judah, from Dan to Beersheba."

L.10: to transfer the kingdom from the house of Saul and to establish the throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan to Beersheba."

R.10: I will take the kingdom away from Saul's family. I will make David king over Israel and Judah, from Dan in the far north to Beersheba in the far south."

decisions.choice: from Dan to Beersheba: the whole land, from north to south
decisions.reason: Dan was the northernmost town of Israel and Beersheba the southernmost; together they name the whole country (Judges 20:1; 1 Samuel 3:20).

decisions.choice: over Israel and over Judah: two parts named separately
decisions.reason: Since Saul's death, Judah had followed David while the other tribes followed Ish-bosheth (2:9-10). Abner promises to bring both under David.

decisions.choice: throne: royal rule
decisions.reason: To establish someone's throne is to make his rule secure.

decisions.choice: make David king
decisions.reason: Readable says what establishing David's throne means.

decisions.choice: in the far north ... in the far south
decisions.reason: Readable explains where the two towns lie, so that the phrase is understood as the whole land.

records.source: וְלֹֽא־יָכֹ֣ל ע֔וֹד לְהָשִׁ֥יב אֶת־אַבְנֵ֖ר דָּבָ֑ר מִיִּרְאָת֖וֹ אֹתֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: And not was able again to return Abner a word, because of his fearing him.
pieces: Ish-bosheth could not say another word in reply to Abner, because he was afraid of him.

L.11: And he could not answer Abner another word, because he feared him.

R.11: Ish-bosheth was so afraid of Abner that he could not say anything back to him.

decisions.choice: to return a word: to answer
decisions.reason: "Bring back a word" is a common way of saying "reply" (1 Kings 12:6).

decisions.choice: he could not ... he feared him: Ish-bosheth feared Abner
decisions.reason: The subject is Ish-bosheth, and "him" is Abner. The king of Israel cannot answer his own commander: the real power lies with Abner.

decisions.choice: Ish-bosheth
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the king, so it is clear who feared whom.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ אַבְנֵ֨ר מַלְאָכִ֧ים׀אֶל־דָּוִ֛ד תַּחְתָּ֥יו לֵאמֹ֖ר לְמִי־אָ֑רֶץ לֵאמֹ֗ר כָּרְתָ֤ה בְרִֽיתְךָ֙ אִתִּ֔י וְהִנֵּה֙ יָדִ֣י עִמָּ֔ךְ לְהָסֵ֥ב אֵלֶ֖יךָ אֶת־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And sent Abner messengers to David on his behalf, saying, To whom [is the] land? Saying, Make your covenant with me, and here, my hand [will be] with you to bring around to you all Israel.
pieces: Abner sent messengers to David on his own behalf to say, "Whose land is it? Make your covenant with me, and I will give you my support to bring all Israel over to you."

L.12: And Abner sent messengers to David on his own behalf, saying, "To whom [does the] land [belong]?" saying, "Make your covenant with me, and look, my hand [will be] with you to bring all Israel around to you."

R.12: Abner sent messengers to David to speak for him. They said, "Who should rule this land? Make a covenant with me, and I will help you. I will bring all Israel over to your side."

decisions.choice: on his own behalf
decisions.reason: The word means "in his place" or "under him". It most likely means that Abner acted for himself, not for Ish-bosheth. It could also mean "on the spot" or "from where he was"; the ancient Greek translation has "to Hebron, where he was". The consonants written in the text and the reading in the margin also differ slightly here.

decisions.choice: to whom does the land belong?: a question that points to David
decisions.reason: The question is short and its point is not spelled out. It most likely means that the land is David's by right, as Yahweh has promised (verses 9, 18). It could also hint that Abner is the one who holds the land and can hand it over.

decisions.choice: covenant: a binding agreement
decisions.reason: A covenant was a formal, sworn agreement between two parties (1 Samuel 18:3; 23:18). Abner asks David to bind himself to him.

decisions.choice: my hand will be with you: I will support you
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power and help. Abner offers to use his influence for David.

decisions.choice: I will give you my support (Balanced); I will help you (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "my hand with you" means.

decisions.choice: Who should rule this land?
decisions.reason: Readable makes the point of the question plain: whose right it is to rule.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ט֔וֹב אֲנִ֕י אֶכְרֹ֥ת אִתְּךָ֖ בְּרִ֑ית אַ֣ךְ דָּבָ֣ר אֶחָ֡ד אָנֹכִי֩ שֹׁאֵ֨ל מֵאִתְּךָ֤ לֵאמֹר֙ לֹא־תִרְאֶ֣ה אֶת־פָּנַ֔י כִּ֣י׀אִם־לִפְנֵ֣י הֱבִיאֲךָ֗ אֵ֚ת מִיכַ֣ל בַּת־שָׁא֔וּל בְּבֹאֲךָ֖ לִרְא֥וֹת אֶת־פָּנָֽי׃ס
records.gloss: And he said, Good; I will make with you a covenant; only one thing I am asking from you, saying, Not you will see my face unless before you bring Michal daughter of Saul when you come to see my face.
pieces: David replied, "Good. I will make a covenant with you. But I require one thing of you: you will not see my face unless you bring Michal daughter of Saul with you when you come to see me."

L.13: And he said, "Good. I will make a covenant with you. Only one thing I ask of you, namely: you will not see my face unless you first bring Michal daughter of Saul when you come to see my face."

R.13: David answered, "Good! I will make a covenant with you. I ask only one thing of you. Do not come to see me unless you bring Saul's daughter Michal with you."

decisions.choice: he said: David answers
decisions.reason: The subject is David, to whom Abner's messengers came (verse 12).

decisions.choice: see my face: come into my presence
decisions.reason: To see a ruler's face is to be received by him (Genesis 43:3, 5; 2 Samuel 14:24). David will not meet Abner without Michal.

decisions.choice: Michal daughter of Saul: David's first wife
decisions.reason: Saul gave Michal to David as his wife (1 Samuel 18:27), but after David fled, Saul gave her to another man (1 Samuel 25:44). Having Saul's daughter back as his wife would also strengthen David's claim, as Saul's son-in-law, to rule over Saul's kingdom.

decisions.choice: unless you first bring: Michal must come before the meeting
decisions.reason: The words mean "unless before that you bring", so Michal's return is the condition for Abner's visit.

decisions.choice: David
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker.

decisions.choice: Do not come to see me unless you bring ... with you
decisions.reason: Readable joins the two mentions of "see my face" into one plain sentence.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח דָּוִד֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל־אִֽישׁ־בֹּ֥שֶׁת בֶּן־שָׁא֖וּל לֵאמֹ֑ר תְּנָ֤ה אֶת־אִשְׁתִּי֙ אֶת־מִיכַ֔ל אֲשֶׁר֙ אֵרַ֣שְׂתִּי לִ֔י בְּמֵאָ֖ה עָרְל֥וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And sent David messengers to Ish-bosheth son of Saul, saying, Give my wife, Michal, whom I betrothed to myself for a hundred foreskins of Philistines.
pieces: Then David sent messengers to Ish-bosheth son of Saul to say, "Give me my wife Michal, whom I won as my bride at the price of a hundred Philistine foreskins."

L.14: And David sent messengers to Ish-bosheth son of Saul, saying, "Give [me] my wife Michal, whom I betrothed to myself for a hundred foreskins of [the] Philistines."

R.14: Then David sent messengers to Saul's son Ish-bosheth. He told them to say, "Give me back my wife Michal. I paid for her with the foreskins of one hundred Philistines."

decisions.choice: David sends to Ish-bosheth: an open, lawful demand
decisions.reason: David does not ask Abner to steal Michal away. He demands her from the king of Saul's house as his lawful wife, and Ish-bosheth gives way (verse 15).

decisions.choice: betrothed to myself: made a binding agreement of marriage
decisions.reason: Betrothal was the agreement, with the bride-price paid, that made a woman a man's wife in law even before they lived together (Deuteronomy 20:7; 22:23-24). David's claim to Michal rests on it.

decisions.choice: a hundred foreskins of Philistines: the bride-price Saul set
decisions.reason: Saul asked a hundred Philistine foreskins as the bride-price (1 Samuel 18:25). David had brought two hundred (1 Samuel 18:27); here he names the price agreed.

decisions.choice: foreskins
decisions.reason: As in 1 Samuel 18:25, the word is kept at every level.

decisions.choice: whom I won as my bride at the price of
decisions.reason: Balanced uses wording that shows both the engagement and the price paid.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ אִ֣ישׁ בֹּ֔שֶׁת וַיִּקָּחֶ֖הָ מֵ֣עִֽם אִ֑ישׁ מֵעִ֖ם פַּלְטִיאֵ֥ל בֶּן־לָֽיִשׁ׃
records.gloss: And sent Ish-bosheth and took her from with [a] husband, from with Paltiel son of Laish.
pieces: So Ish-bosheth sent and took her away from her husband, Paltiel son of Laish.

L.15: And Ish-bosheth sent and took her from [her] husband, from Paltiel son of Laish.

R.15: So Ish-bosheth sent men to take her away from her husband, Paltiel son of Laish.

decisions.choice: Paltiel: the man Saul gave Michal to
decisions.reason: He is called Palti in 1 Samuel 25:44, a shorter form of the same name.

decisions.choice: Laish: the reading noted in the margin
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text spell the father's name differently; the scribes' marginal reading gives Laish, as in 1 Samuel 25:44.

decisions.choice: sent and took her: had her taken
decisions.reason: Ish-bosheth acts through others. He does as David demands, which shows how weak his position has become.

decisions.choice: sent men
decisions.reason: Readable says who carried out the order.

records.source: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ אִתָּ֜הּ אִישָׁ֗הּ הָל֧וֹךְ וּבָכֹ֛ה אַחֲרֶ֖יהָ עַד־בַּֽחֻרִ֑ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֥יו אַבְנֵ֛ר לֵ֥ךְ שׁ֖וּב וַיָּשֹֽׁב׃
records.gloss: And went with her her husband, going and weeping after her, to Bahurim; and said to him Abner, Go, return; and he returned.
pieces: Her husband went with her, weeping as he followed behind her as far as Bahurim. There Abner told him, "Go on, go back." And he went back.

L.16: And her husband went with her, going and weeping behind her, as far as Bahurim. And Abner said to him, "Go, return." And he returned.

R.16: Her husband went along with her. He cried as he walked behind her all the way to the town of Bahurim. Then Abner said to him, "Go home!" So he went home.

decisions.choice: going and weeping: he wept all the way
decisions.reason: The two verbs describe a continuing action. The short sentence lets the reader see what the bargain cost Paltiel.

decisions.choice: Bahurim: a village east of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Bahurim lay on the road from Jerusalem down to the Jordan valley (16:5; 17:18), in Benjamin near the edge of Judah. Paltiel follows Michal to the border of David's territory.

decisions.choice: Abner gives the order
decisions.reason: Abner, not the king, sends Paltiel back. He is in charge of handing Michal over (verse 12).

decisions.choice: the town of Bahurim
decisions.reason: As set for these books, Readable adds "the town of" before a bare place name that could confuse.

records.source: וּדְבַר־אַבְנֵ֣ר הָיָ֔ה עִם־זִקְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר גַּם־תְּמוֹל֙ גַּם־שִׁלְשֹׁ֔ם הֱיִיתֶ֞ם מְבַקְשִׁ֧ים אֶת־דָּוִ֛ד לְמֶ֖לֶךְ עֲלֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And [the] word of Abner was with [the] elders of Israel, saying, Both yesterday and the third day you were seeking David as king over you.
pieces: Abner had talks with the elders of Israel. He said, "For some time now you have wanted David as your king.

L.17: And the word of Abner was with the elders of Israel, saying, "Both yesterday and the day before you have been seeking David [to be] king over you.

R.17: Abner talked with the leaders of Israel. He said, "For a long time now you have wanted David to be your king.

decisions.choice: yesterday and the third day: for some time past
decisions.reason: "Yesterday and the day before" is a common way of saying "before now, for some time" (Exodus 5:8; 1 Samuel 19:7).

decisions.choice: the elders of Israel: the leaders of the tribes
decisions.reason: The elders were the heads of families and clans who spoke for the people. Here "Israel" means the tribes that had followed Ish-bosheth (2:9).

decisions.choice: the word of Abner was with: Abner held talks
decisions.reason: The phrase means that Abner spoke with them and won them over, not that he gave one short message.

decisions.choice: leaders
decisions.reason: Readable says "leaders" for "elders", since the point is their place in the people, not their age.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֖ה עֲשׂ֑וּ כִּ֣י יְהוָ֗ה אָמַ֤ר אֶל־דָּוִד֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בְּיַ֣ד׀דָּוִ֣ד עַבְדִּ֗י הוֹשִׁ֜יעַ אֶת־עַמִּ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מִיַּ֣ד פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וּמִיַּ֖ד כָּל־אֹיְבֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And now act, for Yahweh has said to David, saying, By [the] hand of David my servant save my people Israel from [the] hand of [the] Philistines and from [the] hand of all their enemies.
pieces: Now do it! For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has said of David, 'Through {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David I will rescue {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel from the power of the Philistines and of all their enemies.'"

L.18: And now act! For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken concerning David, saying, 'By the hand of David {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slave I will save {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel from the hand of the Philistines and from the hand of all their enemies.'"

R.18: Now is the time to act! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has said about David, 'I will use {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David to rescue {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel from the Philistines and from all their enemies.'"

decisions.choice: I will save
decisions.reason: The form in the traditional Hebrew text reads like "he saved" or "to save". The sense of Yahweh's promise is "I will save", which a change of one letter gives and which the ancient translations reflect; "to save" gives the same meaning.

decisions.choice: Yahweh has said of David: a promise Abner cites
decisions.reason: No promise in these exact words is recorded earlier. The words echo what Yahweh said of Saul in 1 Samuel 9:16, now applied to David, and fit the choice of David in 1 Samuel 16:1-13.

decisions.choice: by the hand of ... from the hand of: through, from the power of
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for the agent through whom something is done and for the power of an enemy.

decisions.choice: my slave David (Literal); my servant David (Balanced and Readable)
decisions.reason: As set for these books: "slave" at Literal and "servant" at Balanced and Readable. As the LORD's servant, David is one who belongs to him and carries out his will.

decisions.choice: through; from the power of (Balanced); use; from (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the picture of the hand means.

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר גַּם־אַבְנֵ֖ר בְּאָזְנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֑ין וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ גַּם־אַבְנֵ֗ר לְדַבֵּ֞ר בְּאָזְנֵ֤י דָוִד֙ בְּחֶבְר֔וֹן אֵ֤ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־טוֹב֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּבְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל־בֵּ֥ית בִּנְיָמִֽן׃
records.gloss: And spoke also Abner in [the] ears of Benjamin; and went also Abner to speak in [the] ears of David in Hebron all that [was] good in [the] eyes of Israel and in [the] eyes of all [the] house of Benjamin.
pieces: Abner also spoke with the Benjaminites in person. Then he went to Hebron to tell David in person all that Israel and the whole house of Benjamin had agreed to.

L.19: And Abner also spoke in the ears of Benjamin. And Abner also went to speak in the ears of David in Hebron all that [was] good in the eyes of Israel and in the eyes of the whole house of Benjamin.

R.19: Abner also talked with the people of the tribe of Benjamin. Then he went to Hebron to tell David everything that Israel and all the people of Benjamin had agreed to.

decisions.choice: Benjamin: Saul's own tribe
decisions.reason: Saul came from Benjamin (1 Samuel 9:1-2), and his tribe was the most likely to stay loyal to his house. Abner, also of that tribe, speaks with them separately.

decisions.choice: in the ears of: in person, directly
decisions.reason: To speak "in someone's ears" is to tell them face to face.

decisions.choice: good in the eyes of: what they approved
decisions.reason: "Good in the eyes of" means approved or agreed to (1 Samuel 18:5).

decisions.choice: had agreed to
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "good in their eyes" means here.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֨א אַבְנֵ֤ר אֶל־דָּוִד֙ חֶבְר֔וֹן וְאִתּ֖וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים אֲנָשִׁ֑ים וַיַּ֨עַשׂ דָּוִ֧ד לְאַבְנֵ֛ר וְלַאֲנָשִׁ֥ים אֲשֶׁר־אִתּ֖וֹ מִשְׁתֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And came Abner to David [to] Hebron, and with him twenty men; and made David for Abner and for the men who [were] with him a feast.
pieces: When Abner came to David at Hebron with twenty men, David held a feast for Abner and the men with him.

L.20: And Abner came to David at Hebron, and twenty men with him. And David made a feast for Abner and for the men who [were] with him.

R.20: Abner came to David at Hebron with twenty men. David gave a big meal for Abner and his men.

decisions.choice: feast: a meal with drinking that seals an agreement
decisions.reason: The word names a banquet with wine. A shared meal often sealed a covenant (Genesis 26:30; 31:54).

decisions.choice: twenty men: a small escort
decisions.reason: Abner comes with a few men, as an envoy coming in peace, not with an army.

decisions.choice: a big meal
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain word for "feast".

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אַבְנֵ֣ר אֶל־דָּוִ֡ד אָק֣וּמָה׀וְֽאֵלֵ֡כָה וְאֶקְבְּצָה֩ אֶל־אֲדֹנִ֨י הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶת־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְיִכְרְת֤וּ אִתְּךָ֙ בְּרִ֔ית וּמָ֣לַכְתָּ֔ בְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־תְּאַוֶּ֖ה נַפְשֶׁ֑ךָ וַיְּשַׁלַּ֥ח דָּוִ֛ד אֶת־אַבְנֵ֖ר וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ בְּשָׁלֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: And said Abner to David, Let me arise and let me go and let me gather to my lord the king all Israel, and they will make with you a covenant, and you will reign over all that desires your soul. And sent away David Abner, and he went in peace.
pieces: Then Abner said to David, "Let me set out now and gather all Israel to my lord the king, so that they can make a covenant with you, and you will rule over all that you desire." So David sent Abner away, and he went in peace.

L.21: And Abner said to David, "Let me arise and go and gather all Israel to my lord the king, so that they may make a covenant with you, and you will reign over all that your soul desires." And David sent Abner away, and he went in peace.

R.21: Then Abner said to David, "Let me go now and bring all the people of Israel together for you, my master the king. They will make a covenant with you, and you will be king over everything you want." So David let Abner go, and he left in peace.

decisions.choice: my lord the king: Abner speaks as David's subject
decisions.reason: Abner now calls David by the title he used for Saul (1 Samuel 17:55). He has changed sides.

decisions.choice: all that your soul desires: whatever you wish
decisions.reason: "Soul" here is the inner self with its longings. Abner promises David the whole kingdom he hopes for; compare 1 Kings 11:37.

decisions.choice: in peace: safely, under an agreement
decisions.reason: "In peace" means safe and unharmed, on good terms. The phrase comes three times (verses 21, 22, 23), making clear that David meant Abner no harm.

decisions.choice: Let me set out now
decisions.reason: "Arise and go" means to start out; Balanced says so.

decisions.choice: my master
decisions.reason: Readable uses "master" for "lord" when one person addresses another, so that it is not confused with the title for God.

records.source: וְהִנֵּה֩ עַבְדֵ֨י דָוִ֤ד וְיוֹאָב֙ בָּ֣א מֵֽהַגְּד֔וּד וְשָׁלָ֥ל רָ֖ב עִמָּ֣ם הֵבִ֑יאוּ וְאַבְנֵ֗ר אֵינֶ֤נּוּ עִם־דָּוִד֙ בְּחֶבְר֔וֹן כִּ֥י שִׁלְּח֖וֹ וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ בְּשָׁלֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: And here, [the] servants of David and Joab came from the raid, and plunder much with them they brought; and Abner not with David in Hebron, for he had sent him away, and he had gone in peace.
pieces: Just then David's men and Joab came back from a raid, bringing a great deal of plunder with them. But Abner was no longer with David in Hebron, because David had sent him away and he had gone in peace.

L.22: And look, the servants of David and Joab came from the raid, and they brought much plunder with them. But Abner [was] not with David in Hebron, for he had sent him away, and he had gone in peace.

R.22: Just then Joab and David's soldiers came back from a raid. They brought back many things they had captured. But Abner was no longer with David in Hebron. David had let him go, and he had left in peace.

decisions.choice: and look: a turn in the story
decisions.reason: The word draws attention to a new arrival at just the wrong moment: Joab returns right after Abner has left.

decisions.choice: the servants of David: David's fighting men
decisions.reason: Here "servants" are the soldiers who followed David, as in 2:12-17 and 2:30-31.

decisions.choice: Joab came: the verb is singular
decisions.reason: The verb agrees with Joab alone, putting him in the foreground; he is the one whose coming matters.

decisions.choice: servants (Literal); men (Balanced); soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word usually means "slave" or "servant", but here it names David's soldiers, so Balanced and Readable say so.

records.source: וְיוֹאָ֛ב וְכָל־הַצָּבָ֥א אֲשֶׁר־אִתּ֖וֹ בָּ֑אוּ וַיַּגִּ֤דוּ לְיוֹאָב֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בָּֽא־אַבְנֵ֤ר בֶּן־נֵר֙ אֶל־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֵ֖הוּ וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ בְּשָׁלֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: And Joab and all the army which [was] with him came, and they told Joab, saying, Came Abner son of Ner to the king, and he sent him away, and he went in peace.
pieces: When Joab and all the army with him arrived, Joab was told, "Abner son of Ner came to the king, and the king sent him away, and he has gone in peace."

L.23: And Joab and all the army that [was] with him came, and they told Joab, saying, "Abner son of Ner came to the king, and he sent him away, and he has gone in peace."

R.23: When Joab and all his troops arrived, someone told him, "Abner son of Ner came to see the king. The king let him go, and he has left in peace."

decisions.choice: they told Joab: Joab was told
decisions.reason: The plural "they" has no named subject; it means that people told him.

decisions.choice: Abner son of Ner: the man who killed Joab's brother
decisions.reason: Abner had killed Asahel, Joab's brother, in the fighting at Gibeon (2:18-23). The news brings that back; see verse 27.

decisions.choice: the king sent him away
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the king, so "he sent him away" is not unclear.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֤א יוֹאָב֙ אֶל־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מֶ֣ה עָשִׂ֑יתָה הִנֵּה־בָ֤א אַבְנֵר֙ אֵלֶ֔יךָ לָמָּה־זֶּ֥ה שִׁלַּחְתּ֖וֹ וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ הָלֽוֹךְ׃
records.gloss: And came Joab to the king and said, What have you done? Here, came Abner to you; why this [that] you sent him away, and he has gone, going?
pieces: Joab went in to the king. "What have you done?" he said. "Abner came to you! Why did you send him away? Now he has got clean away!

L.24: And Joab came to the king and said, "What have you done? Look, Abner came to you! Why [is] this, [that] you sent him away, and he has gone, really gone?

R.24: So Joab went to see the king. He said, "What have you done? Abner came to you! Why did you let him go? Now he has gotten away!

decisions.choice: he has gone, going: he is gone for good
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis: Abner has gone and is now out of reach.

decisions.choice: what have you done? why did you send him away?: a rebuke
decisions.reason: Joab's questions are not requests for information but sharp blame, spoken to the king without respect.

decisions.choice: got clean away (Balanced); gotten away (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the force of the doubled verb in natural wording.

records.source: יָדַ֨עְתָּ֙ אֶת־אַבְנֵ֣ר בֶּן־נֵ֔ר כִּ֥י לְפַתֹּתְךָ֖ בָּ֑א וְלָדַ֜עַת אֶת־מוֹצָֽאֲךָ֙ וְאֶת־מ֣וֹבָאֶ֔ךָ וְלָדַ֕עַת אֵ֛ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתָּ֖ה עֹשֶֽׂה׃
records.gloss: You know Abner son of Ner, that to deceive you he came, and to know your going out and your coming in, and to know all that you are doing.
pieces: You know Abner son of Ner! He came to deceive you, to learn all your movements and find out everything you are doing."

L.25: You know Abner son of Ner, that he came to deceive you, and to know your going out and your coming in, and to know all that you are doing."

R.25: You know what Abner son of Ner is like. He came here to trick you. He wanted to find out where you go and everything you are doing."

decisions.choice: your going out and your coming in: all your movements
decisions.reason: The pair covers all of a person's activity, especially a leader's plans in war (1 Samuel 18:13, 16; 29:6).

decisions.choice: your coming in: the reading noted in the margin
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text and the scribes' marginal reading differ only in the spelling of this word. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: to deceive you: to lead you on with false words
decisions.reason: The verb means to entice or fool someone. Whether Joab believes his own charge is left open; verse 27 gives his real motive.

decisions.choice: where you go
decisions.reason: Readable says what the pair of words means.

records.source: וַיֵּצֵ֤א יוֹאָב֙ מֵעִ֣ם דָּוִ֔ד וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח מַלְאָכִים֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י אַבְנֵ֔ר וַיָּשִׁ֥בוּ אֹת֖וֹ מִבּ֣וֹר הַסִּרָ֑ה וְדָוִ֖ד לֹ֥א יָדָֽע׃
records.gloss: And went out Joab from with David and sent messengers after Abner, and they brought him back from [the] cistern of Sirah; and David did not know.
pieces: After leaving David, Joab sent messengers to go after Abner, and they fetched him back from the well of Sirah. David knew nothing of this.

L.26: And Joab went out from David and sent messengers after Abner, and they brought him back from the cistern of Sirah. But David did not know.

R.26: Joab left David and sent messengers to go after Abner. They brought him back from the well of Sirah. David knew nothing about this.

decisions.choice: the cistern of Sirah: a well or cistern on the road north of Hebron
decisions.reason: The word can mean a cistern cut in rock or a well. The place is mentioned only here, and its site is not certain; it must have been a short way from Hebron.

decisions.choice: David did not know: the narrator clears David
decisions.reason: The writer says plainly that David had no part in what followed. Verses 28 and 37 make the same point.

decisions.choice: the well of Sirah
decisions.reason: "Well" is the more familiar word for a place where travelers stopped for water.

records.source: וַיָּ֤שָׁב אַבְנֵר֙ חֶבְר֔וֹן וַיַּטֵּ֤הוּ יוֹאָב֙ אֶל־תּ֣וֹךְ הַשַּׁ֔עַר לְדַבֵּ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ בַּשֶּׁ֑לִי וַיַּכֵּ֤הוּ שָׁם֙ הַחֹ֔מֶשׁ וַיָּ֕מָת בְּדַ֖ם עֲשָׂה־אֵ֥ל אָחִֽיו׃
records.gloss: And returned Abner [to] Hebron, and turned him aside Joab into [the] middle of the gate to speak with him in quiet, and struck him there [in] the belly, and he died, for [the] blood of Asahel his brother.
pieces: When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab took him aside into the gateway, as if to speak with him privately. There he stabbed him in the belly, and Abner died, in revenge for the blood of Joab's brother Asahel.

L.27: And Abner returned to Hebron, and Joab took him aside into the middle of the gate to speak with him in private, and he struck him there [in] the belly, and he died for the blood of Asahel his brother.

R.27: When Abner came back to Hebron, Joab took him to one side inside the city gate. He acted as if he wanted to talk with him alone. Then Joab stabbed Abner in the belly, and Abner died. Joab did this to pay Abner back for killing his brother Asahel.

decisions.choice: the middle of the gate: inside the gateway
decisions.reason: A city gate was a passage with rooms on each side, where people met and business was done. Joab draws Abner into it, away from the open street. The ancient Greek translation has "the side of the gate"; either way, the place was out of public view.

decisions.choice: struck him in the belly: as Abner had struck Asahel
decisions.reason: The same word for "belly" is used where Abner killed Asahel with the butt of his spear (2:23). Joab kills Abner the same way.

decisions.choice: for the blood of Asahel: blood revenge
decisions.reason: A close relative was expected to avenge a killing (Numbers 35:19). But Asahel died in battle, chasing Abner, who had warned him twice (2:19-23), and Hebron was one of the cities of refuge (Joshua 20:7; 21:13). Joab's revenge is presented as murder, as David's words in verses 28-29 and 39 show.

decisions.choice: in private: quietly, alone
decisions.reason: The word means quietness. Joab pretends to want a private word, which is how he catches Abner off guard.

decisions.choice: as if to speak (Balanced); He acted as if he wanted to talk (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "to speak with him in private", but what follows shows that this was a pretense. Balanced and Readable make that clear.

decisions.choice: to pay Abner back for killing his brother Asahel
decisions.reason: Readable says what "for the blood of" means.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע דָּוִד֙ מֵאַ֣חֲרֵי כֵ֔ן וַיֹּ֗אמֶר נָקִ֨י אָנֹכִ֧י וּמַמְלַכְתִּ֛י מֵעִ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה עַד־עוֹלָ֑ם מִדְּמֵ֖י אַבְנֵ֥ר בֶּן־נֵֽר׃
records.gloss: And heard David from afterward thus, and said, Innocent [am] I and my kingdom from with Yahweh until forever of [the] blood of Abner son of Ner.
pieces: Afterward, when David heard of it, he said, "Before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, I and my kingdom are innocent of the blood of Abner son of Ner for all time.

L.28: And David heard [of it] afterward, and he said, "I and my kingdom [are] innocent before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} forever of the blood of Abner son of Ner.

R.28: Later David heard what had happened. He said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} knows that my kingdom and I are not guilty of the death of Abner son of Ner, and we never will be.

decisions.choice: innocent of the blood: not guilty of the killing
decisions.reason: "Blood" stands for a killing and the guilt that comes with it (Deuteronomy 19:10; 21:8-9). David declares that he did not cause or approve Abner's death.

decisions.choice: before Yahweh: in Yahweh's judgment
decisions.reason: The words mean "from Yahweh's side": Yahweh, who sees all, holds David free of guilt.

decisions.choice: I and my kingdom: guilt could rest on a king's house and land
decisions.reason: Guilt for blood could fall on a whole family and on the land (21:1; Deuteronomy 21:1-9). David clears both himself and his kingdom.

decisions.choice: The LORD knows
decisions.reason: Readable turns "innocent before the LORD" into a plain statement of what the LORD sees.

records.source: יָחֻ֨לוּ֙ עַל־רֹ֣אשׁ יוֹאָ֔ב וְאֶ֖ל כָּל־בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֑יו וְֽאַל־יִכָּרֵ֣ת מִבֵּ֣ית יוֹאָ֡ב זָ֠ב וּמְצֹרָ֞ע וּמַחֲזִ֥יק בַּפֶּ֛לֶךְ וְנֹפֵ֥ל בַּחֶ֖רֶב וַחֲסַר־לָֽחֶם׃
records.gloss: May they whirl on [the] head of Joab and on all [the] house of his father; and may not be cut off from [the] house of Joab [one] having a discharge, and [one with] scale disease, and [one] holding a spindle, and [one] falling by the sword, and [one] lacking bread.
pieces: May the guilt come down on Joab's head and on his father's whole house! May Joab's family never be without someone who has a discharge or a serious skin disease, or who holds a spindle, or who falls by the sword, or who lacks food!"

L.29: May it whirl onto the head of Joab and onto all his father's house; and may there never be lacking from the house of Joab one who has a discharge, or one with scale disease, or one who holds a spindle, or one who falls by the sword, or one who lacks bread!"

R.29: May the guilt for Abner's death fall on Joab and on all his family! May there always be someone in Joab's family who has a discharge from his body, or a serious skin disease, or who must do women's work like spinning, or who is killed in battle, or who does not have enough to eat!"

decisions.choice: may it whirl: the subject is the guilt for the blood
decisions.reason: The verb is plural, picking up the word "blood" in verse 28, which has a plural form. The guilt for Abner's death is to come down on Joab.

decisions.choice: whirl: come down hard
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a storm that whirls and bursts on someone's head (Jeremiah 23:19). David prays that the guilt will strike Joab with force.

decisions.choice: one who holds a spindle: a man fit only for women's work
alternatives: one who leans on a crutch
decisions.reason: The word means a spindle, the tool used in spinning thread, which was women's work (Proverbs 31:19). A man who held one would be one unable to fight or work as men did. Some take the word as "crutch", meaning a man who is lame. Either way, the curse wishes weakness on Joab's line.

decisions.choice: a discharge, scale disease: conditions that made a person unclean
decisions.reason: Both are described in the law (Leviticus 13; 15). Those who had them were unclean and could be shut out of normal life. Together with weakness, violent death and hunger, they make a curse of shame and want on Joab's family.

decisions.choice: the guilt
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name what will fall on Joab, since the verb's subject comes from the previous verse.

decisions.choice: scale disease (Literal); a serious skin disease (Balanced and Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 13-14.

decisions.choice: who must do women's work like spinning
decisions.reason: Readable says what holding a spindle stands for. See the meaning decision; this explanation follows the reading chosen there.

records.source: וְיוֹאָב֙ וַאֲבִישַׁ֣י אָחִ֔יו הָרְג֖וּ לְאַבְנֵ֑ר עַל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֵמִ֜ית אֶת־עֲשָׂהאֵ֧ל אֲחִיהֶ֛ם בְּגִבְע֖וֹן בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And Joab and Abishai his brother killed Abner, because he had put to death Asahel their brother at Gibeon in the battle.
pieces: So it was that Joab and his brother Abishai killed Abner, for he had put their brother Asahel to death in the battle at Gibeon.

L.30: And Joab and Abishai his brother killed Abner, because he had put to death Asahel their brother at Gibeon in the battle.

R.30: Joab and his brother Abishai killed Abner because Abner had killed their brother Asahel in the battle at Gibeon.

decisions.choice: Joab and Abishai: the narrator names both brothers
decisions.reason: Joab struck the blow (verse 27), but the narrator holds Abishai responsible with him; both were Asahel's brothers. David speaks of "the sons of Zeruiah" in verse 39.

decisions.choice: at Gibeon in the battle: the fighting of 2:12-32
decisions.reason: Asahel was killed during the battle at the pool of Gibeon, when he pursued Abner (2:18-23). The narrator reminds the reader that it was a death in war.

decisions.choice: because Abner had killed
decisions.reason: Readable names Abner so that "he" is not unclear.

records.source: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ דָּוִ֨ד אֶל־יוֹאָ֜ב וְאֶל־כָּל־הָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־אִתּ֗וֹ קִרְע֤וּ בִגְדֵיכֶם֙ וְחִגְר֣וּ שַׂקִּ֔ים וְסִפְד֖וּ לִפְנֵ֣י אַבְנֵ֑ר וְהַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֔ד הֹלֵ֖ךְ אַחֲרֵ֥י הַמִּטָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And said David to Joab and to all the people who [were] with him, Tear your garments and gird on sackcloth and mourn before Abner. And the king David [was] walking behind the bier.
pieces: Then David told Joab and all the people who were with him, "Tear your clothes, wrap yourselves in sackcloth, and mourn as you walk ahead of Abner." And King David himself walked behind the bier.

L.31: And David said to Joab and to all the people who [were] with him, "Tear your clothes and put on sackcloth and mourn before Abner." And King David walked behind the bier.

R.31: Then David told Joab and all the people with him, "Tear your clothes and wear sackcloth. Mourn for Abner as you walk ahead of his body." King David himself walked behind the frame that carried the body.

decisions.choice: tear your clothes, put on sackcloth, mourn: the signs of mourning
decisions.reason: Tearing one's clothes and wearing sackcloth, a rough cloth of goat's hair, showed grief in public (Genesis 37:34; 2 Samuel 1:11-12).

decisions.choice: the bier: the frame on which a body was carried
decisions.reason: The dead were carried to burial on an open frame or stretcher, not in a closed coffin.

decisions.choice: David makes Joab mourn: a public sign
decisions.reason: David orders Joab himself to mourn, and the king walks behind the body. All the people can see that David honors Abner and rejects what was done to him (verses 36-37).

decisions.choice: as you walk ahead of Abner (Balanced); as you walk ahead of his body (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Before Abner" here means in front of the bier in the funeral procession, since the king walked behind it.

decisions.choice: the frame that carried the body
decisions.reason: Readable explains "bier", a word many readers do not know.

records.heading: David mourns for Abner

records.source: וַיִּקְבְּר֥וּ אֶת־אַבְנֵ֖ר בְּחֶבְר֑וֹן וַיִשָּׂ֧אהַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אֶת־קוֹל֗וֹ וַיֵּבְךְּ֙ אֶל־קֶ֣בֶר אַבְנֵ֔ר וַיִּבְכּ֖וּ כָּל־הָעָֽם׃פ
records.gloss: And they buried Abner in Hebron; and lifted the king his voice and wept at [the] grave of Abner, and wept all the people.
pieces: They buried Abner in Hebron, and the king wept aloud at Abner's grave, and all the people wept too.

L.32: And they buried Abner in Hebron. And the king lifted up his voice and wept at the grave of Abner, and all the people wept.

R.32: They buried Abner in Hebron. The king cried loudly at Abner's grave, and all the people cried too.

decisions.choice: lifted up his voice and wept: wept aloud
decisions.reason: The phrase describes loud, open weeping (Genesis 29:11; 1 Samuel 24:17).

decisions.choice: buried in Hebron: in David's own city
decisions.reason: Abner was a man of Benjamin, but he was buried in Hebron, where David reigned. The burial in the king's city was an honor.

decisions.choice: wept aloud
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of the idiom.

records.source: וַיְקֹנֵ֥ן הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אֶל־אַבְנֵ֖ר וַיֹּאמַ֑ר הַכְּמ֥וֹת נָבָ֖ל יָמ֥וּת אַבְנֵֽר׃
records.gloss: And lamented the king for Abner and said, As [the] death of a fool should die Abner?
pieces: The king sang a lament for Abner. He said, \q "Should Abner have died as a fool dies?

L.33: And the king lamented for Abner and said, \q "Should Abner die as a fool dies?

R.33: The king sang a sad song about Abner. He said, \q "Should Abner have died the way a fool dies?

decisions.choice: lamented: sang a funeral song
decisions.reason: The verb means to chant a lament, a set poem of mourning for the dead, as David did for Saul and Jonathan (1:17).

decisions.choice: a fool: a senseless, worthless man
decisions.reason: The word names a man without sense or moral worth, who brings ruin on himself; it is the name of Nabal in 1 Samuel 25:25. Abner, a great warrior, died unarmed and off guard, the kind of death such a man might meet.

decisions.choice: should Abner die ...?: a question that expects "no"
decisions.reason: The question is a cry of grief: Abner did not deserve such a death.

decisions.choice: the lament set in lines
decisions.reason: David's lament (verses 33b-34a) is poetry and is set in lines. The first line of each verse is the narrator's.

records.source: יָדֶ֣ךָ לֹֽא־אֲסֻר֗וֹת וְרַגְלֶ֨יךָ֙ לֹא־לִנְחֻשְׁתַּ֣יִם הֻגָּ֔שׁוּ כִּנְפ֛וֹל לִפְנֵ֥י בְנֵֽי־עַוְלָ֖ה נָפָ֑לְתָּ וַיֹּסִ֥פוּ כָל־הָעָ֖ם לִבְכּ֥וֹת עָלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: Your hands not bound, and your feet not to bronze [fetters] brought near; as falls [one] before sons of injustice you fell. And added all the people to weep over him.
pieces: Your hands were not tied, your feet were not put in chains of bronze; \q as one falls before wicked men, so you fell." \q And all the people wept over him again.

L.34: Your hands [were] not bound, and your feet were not put into fetters of bronze; \q as one falls before sons of injustice, you fell." \q And all the people wept over him again.

R.34: Your hands were not tied, and your feet were not in chains. \q You fell like someone killed by evil men." \q Then all the people cried over Abner again.

decisions.choice: hands not bound, feet not in fetters: Abner was no prisoner
decisions.reason: Abner did not die as a captive or a condemned man, nor did he fall fighting. He was free and unsuspecting, and he was killed by treachery.

decisions.choice: fetters of bronze: a pair of bronze shackles
decisions.reason: The word has a form meaning a pair, the shackles put on a prisoner's feet (Judges 16:21).

decisions.choice: sons of injustice: wicked men
decisions.reason: "Sons of" a quality means people marked by it (7:10). Abner fell the way a man falls to criminals.

decisions.choice: chains
decisions.reason: Readable says "chains" without naming the metal.

decisions.choice: Abner
decisions.reason: Readable names Abner for "him".

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֣א כָל־הָעָ֗ם לְהַבְר֧וֹת אֶת־דָּוִ֛ד לֶ֖חֶם בְּע֣וֹד הַיּ֑וֹם וַיִּשָּׁבַ֨ע דָּוִ֜ד לֵאמֹ֗ר כֹּ֣ה יַעֲשֶׂה־לִּ֤י אֱלֹהִים֙ וְכֹ֣ה יֹסִ֔יף כִּ֣י אִם־לִפְנֵ֧י בֽוֹא־הַשֶּׁ֛מֶשׁ אֶטְעַם־לֶ֖חֶם א֥וֹ כָל־מְאֽוּמָה׃
records.gloss: And came all the people to cause to eat David bread while still the day; and swore David, saying, Thus may do to me God and thus may he add, if before goes the sun I taste bread or anything.
pieces: Then all the people came to urge David to eat some food while it was still day. But David took an oath: "May God deal with me ever so severely if I taste bread or any other food before sunset!"

L.35: And all the people came to make David eat bread while it was still day. But David swore, saying, "Thus may God do to me, and thus may {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} add, if before the sun goes down I taste bread or anything at all!"

R.35: All the people came to get David to eat something while it was still daytime. But David made a promise. He said, "May God punish me terribly if I eat bread or anything else before the sun goes down!"

decisions.choice: to make David eat: the meal brought to a mourner
decisions.reason: Friends brought food to those in mourning and urged them to eat (Jeremiah 16:7). The verb is the one used for giving food to the sick or grieving (13:5-6). David refuses and fasts until evening, as he did for Saul (1:12).

decisions.choice: thus may God do to me, and thus may he add: a curse on oneself
decisions.reason: As in verse 9.

decisions.choice: bread or anything: any food at all
decisions.reason: "Bread" stands for food in general; "anything" makes the oath complete.

decisions.choice: May God deal with me ever so severely if
decisions.reason: As in verse 9 and 1 Samuel 20:13.

records.source: וְכָל־הָעָ֣ם הִכִּ֔ירוּ וַיִּיטַ֖ב בְּעֵֽינֵיהֶ֑ם כְּכֹל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֣ה הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ בְּעֵינֵ֥י כָל־הָעָ֖ם טֽוֹב׃
records.gloss: And all the people took note, and it was good in their eyes; as all that the king did in [the] eyes of all the people [was] good.
pieces: All the people took note of it, and it pleased them, just as everything the king did pleased all the people.

L.36: And all the people took note, and it was good in their eyes, as everything that the king did was good in the eyes of all the people.

R.36: All the people saw what David did, and they were pleased. In fact, everything the king did pleased them.

decisions.choice: good in their eyes: it pleased them
decisions.reason: As in verse 19.

decisions.choice: as everything the king did: a general statement
decisions.reason: The words widen the point: the people approved of David's conduct in this as in all he did.

decisions.choice: In fact, everything the king did
decisions.reason: Readable makes a new sentence of the general statement.

records.source: וַיֵּדְע֧וּ כָל־הָעָ֛ם וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא כִּ֣י לֹ֤א הָיְתָה֙ מֵֽהַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לְהָמִ֖ית אֶת־אַבְנֵ֥ר בֶּן־נֵֽר׃פ
records.gloss: And knew all the people and all Israel on that day that not it was from the king to kill Abner son of Ner.
pieces: So all the people and all Israel understood that day that the king had no part in the killing of Abner son of Ner.

L.37: And all the people and all Israel knew on that day that it had not been from the king to put Abner son of Ner to death.

R.37: That day all the people, and all Israel too, understood that the king had not wanted Abner son of Ner to be killed.

decisions.choice: all the people and all Israel: those with David and the northern tribes
decisions.reason: "The people" are those who were at the burial in Hebron (verses 31-36); "all Israel" are the tribes that had followed Ish-bosheth and Abner. Both understood that David was not to blame.

decisions.choice: it was not from the king: it was not his doing
decisions.reason: To say that something was "from" someone means that it came from his will or order.

decisions.choice: the king had not wanted
decisions.reason: Readable says the same thing in plain words: the killing was not what David wanted.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל־עֲבָדָ֑יו הֲל֣וֹא תֵדְע֔וּ כִּי־שַׂ֣ר וְגָד֗וֹל נָפַ֛ל הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And said the king to his servants, Do not you know that a prince and a great [man] has fallen this day in Israel?
pieces: Then the king said to his officials, "Do you not realize that a leader and a great man has fallen in Israel today?

L.38: And the king said to his servants, "Do you not know that a prince and a great [man] has fallen this day in Israel?

R.38: Then the king said to his officials, "You must know that a great leader has died in Israel today.

decisions.choice: prince: a man of high rank
decisions.reason: The word names a ruler or high officer. Abner had been commander of Saul's army (1 Samuel 14:50) and the most powerful man in Ish-bosheth's kingdom.

decisions.choice: has fallen: has been killed
decisions.reason: "Fall" is used of a violent death, as in David's lament for Saul and Jonathan (1:19, 25, 27).

decisions.choice: do you not know?: a question that expects "yes"
decisions.reason: The question is a way of saying "surely you know".

decisions.choice: officials

decisions.choice: prince (Literal); leader (Balanced); great leader (Readable)

decisions.choice: You must know

records.gloss: And I this day [am] weak, and anointed king; and the men, these, [the] sons of Zeruiah, [are] too hard for me. May repay Yahweh to [the] doer of the evil according to his evil.
pieces: Today I am weak, even though I am anointed king, and these men, the sons of Zeruiah, are too harsh for me. May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} repay the one who does evil as his evil deserves!"

L.39: And I [am] weak this day, though anointed king; and these men, the sons of Zeruiah, [are] too hard for me. May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} repay the doer of evil according to his evil!"

R.39: Today I am weak, even though I have been anointed as king. These sons of Zeruiah, Joab and Abishai, are too violent for me to control. May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} pay back the evil man for the evil he has done!"

decisions.choice: weak: lacking power
decisions.reason: The word means soft or tender. Here, set against "hard" later in the verse, it means that David does not yet have the strength to act against Joab and his brother.

decisions.choice: and anointed king: though anointed
decisions.reason: The "and" joins two things that do not fit together: David is the anointed king, yet he is not strong enough to punish his own commanders.

decisions.choice: the sons of Zeruiah: Joab and Abishai
decisions.reason: Zeruiah was David's sister (1 Chronicles 2:16), so Joab, Abishai and Asahel were David's nephews.

decisions.choice: may Yahweh repay: David leaves vengeance to Yahweh
decisions.reason: As before with Saul (1 Samuel 24:13; 26:10), David leaves judgment to Yahweh. Later he charges Solomon to deal with Joab (1 Kings 2:5-6).

decisions.choice: Joab and Abishai
decisions.reason: Readable names the sons of Zeruiah.

decisions.choice: too harsh (Balanced); too violent for me to control (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Hard" here means ruthless and hard to restrain; Balanced and Readable say so.
